overview: The Medford City Council supported unionization efforts by Tufts University resident assistants, approved funding and classification for a new senior planner position, and finalized a personnel ordinance for the library union. The council also addressed municipal finance reporting concerns, website improvements, and winter energy assistance.

items.title: Tufts Resident Assistants Union Resolution
items.summary: Approved a resolution expressing support for the United Labor of Tufts Resident Assistants and calling on Tufts University to voluntarily recognize their union.

items.title: Finance Director Salary Appropriation
items.summary: Referred back to the mayor's office an appropriation of $1,205 to correct a clerical error regarding the effective date of the finance director's step increase, following debate over overdue municipal financial reports.

items.title: Condolences and Babe Kelowna Day
items.summary: Passed a condolence resolution for William Matarazzo and proclaimed Michael Babe Kelowna Day in honor of a 50-year-old Thanksgiving football record ahead of the Medford-Malden game.

items.title: Resident Parking List and Website Review
items.summary: Approved resolutions requesting an update to the municipal website's list of permit parking streets and scheduling a Committee of the Whole meeting to review resident feedback on website improvements.

items.title: Winter Home Heating and Energy Assistance
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting an update from the planning director on local programs available to assist residents with rising heating and energy costs.

items.title: Secondhand Articles License for Pro Repair
items.summary: Approved with conditions a secondhand articles license for Pro Repair at 19 Salem Street, limiting sales and repairs to phones, tablets, and computers.

items.title: Senior Planner Position and Classification
items.summary: Approved an appropriation of $55,267 and third reading of an ordinance establishing a senior planner position, following debate over citywide staffing vacancies and expired municipal labor contracts.

items.title: Library Union Personnel Ordinance
items.summary: Approved the third reading of a personnel ordinance reflecting the negotiated collective bargaining agreement for the library union.
